Slack is a firehose of information with feeds of messages streaming in from all over.  
  
In those streams are needle in the haystack messages you'd want to act on instantly if only you knew about them.

 the urgent support message
 the high-value sign-up
 the error log from that one particular part of your product

Historically, it's been too expensive and slow to run LLM's on every Slack message, but with the release of Jev that's changed!  
  
Slack Lookout uses Jev to inject real-time intelligence into every Slack channel of your choice.  
  
It's meant to be pretty simple: [...] 1. Write in plain english what it should lookout for and which channels to look in.
2. Using Jev, Lookout will evaluate every message for that thing.
3. If it matches, Lookout will send a DM, an email, open a Linear ticket, or more.

Review Jev?

Reviewers, all of them founders, describe Jev as a strong fit for software tasks that need fast, structured judgments rather than open-ended text. Makers of Famulor say it keeps live-call agents responsive, while Bevel says demand for Jev-style automation was strong enough to inspire a GDPR-friendly alternative. Others repeatedly praise the calibrated probabilities, simple API, and lower cost, with concrete uses in quality checks, moderation, and recommendation workflows where teams set thresholds and keep decisions traceable.

gg-friggin-ez

used Jev to build gg-friggin-ez instead of OpenAI

•2 reviews

General-purpose generative LLMs can be too slow and expensive to run on every live-chat message. OpenAI's omni-moderation model is genuinely good at general moderation, but starts missing things on obfuscated text, romanized Indic, and the usual game chat evasion tricks. Jev returns calibrated probabilities/scores for toxicity, profanity, severity, language, and obfuscation type. gg-friggin-ez then applies deterministic policy thresholds to produce ALLOW / SUSPICIOUS\_REVIEW / AUTO\_CENSOR / AUTO\_BAN.
